test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A gardener increases the area of his rectangular garden by increasing its length by 40% and decreasing its breadth by 20%. The area of the new garden is what percentage more than the area of the old garden?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Percentage Change** formula: Net Change = x + y + (x × y)/100

Here, increase in length (x) = +40 and decrease in breadth (y) = −20

Net change in Area = 40 − 20 + [40 × (−20)] / 100

Net change in Area = 20 − 8 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in **Length** = 40%

Decrease in **Breadth** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rectangle = Length × Breadth

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b5b2cb7c5ab4c0deb89e17e109e70e246998bcf9b5942a51902ddc956fa8dc9b.png] 

⇒ Let the initial **Length** be 10 units and initial **Breadth** be 10 units.

⇒ Initial Area = 10 × 10 = 100 units²

⇒ New Length = 10 + (40% of 10) = 14 units

⇒ New Breadth = 10 − (20% of 10) = 8 units

⇒ New Area = 14 × 8 = 112 units²

⇒ Percentage change = [(New Area − Initial Area) / Initial Area] × 100

⇒ Percentage change = [(112 − 100) / 100] × 100 = 12%

**∴ The correct answer is 12%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the overall percentage change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Area and Multipliers

Percentage changes can be solved using decimal multipliers. An increase of 40% is × 1.4 and a decrease of 20% is × 0.8. The result is 1.4 × 0.8 = 1.12, representing a 12% increase.

Product Stability Rule

If the product (Area) remains constant while one factor (Length) increases by x%, the other factor (Breadth) must decrease by [x / (100 + x)] × 100%.</p
